faq.question: What is IVF and who is it for?
faq.answer: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) is a process where an egg is combined with sperm outside the body, in a lab. It's a primary treatment for infertility for couples who have been unable to conceive naturally.

faq.question: What is the success rate of IVF at your center?
faq.answer: Our IVF center has a high success rate of 72%, which is above the national average. Success rates can vary based on factors like age and cause of infertility.

faq.question: How long does one IVF cycle take?
faq.answer: A complete IVF cycle typically takes about four to six weeks, from the start of ovarian stimulation until the pregnancy test.

faq.question: Is the IVF process painful?
faq.answer: Most patients experience minimal discomfort. Procedures like egg retrieval are performed under mild sedation to ensure you are comfortable.

faq.question: When should I consider joint replacement surgery?
faq.answer: Joint replacement is typically recommended when joint pain and stiffness severely limit your daily activities, and non-surgical treatments like medication, physical therapy, and injections are no longer effective. Our specialists will provide a thorough evaluation to determine if you're a candidate.

faq.question: What is recovery like after arthroscopic surgery?
faq.answer: Recovery from arthroscopic surgery is much faster than open surgery. Most patients can go home the same day and return to light activities within a few days. Full recovery typically takes a few weeks to months depending on the specific procedure and your compliance with rehabilitation.

faq.question: How long do joint replacements last?
faq.answer: Modern joint replacements can last 15-20 years or more with proper care. The longevity depends on factors like your activity level, age, weight, and the type of implant used. Our surgeons use the latest implant technology for optimal durability.

faq.question: Do you treat sports injuries?

faq.question: What are the common symptoms of a urinary tract infection (UTI)?
faq.answer: Common symptoms include a frequent urge to urinate, a burning sensation during urination, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, and pelvic pain. If you experience these symptoms, it is important to consult a urologist.

faq.question: How are kidney stones treated?
faq.answer: Treatment for kidney stones depends on their size and location. Small stones may pass on their own, while larger stones may require procedures like laser lithotripsy (breaking stones with a laser) or ESWL (shock wave therapy).

faq.question: What is the recovery time for prostate surgery?
faq.answer: Recovery time varies depending on the type of procedure. Minimally invasive procedures like laser prostatectomy typically have shorter recovery times of 1-2 weeks, while traditional surgery may require 4-6 weeks.

faq.question: What is a Level III NICU?
faq.answer: A Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) is equipped to care for very small or very sick newborn babies. We have a full range of specialists, advanced equipment, and can handle the most complex neonatal cases including those requiring surgery or mechanical ventilation.

faq.question: Can parents stay with their baby in the NICU?
faq.answer: Yes, we encourage parents to be with their baby as much as possible. We provide 24/7 family access, comfortable seating areas, and family accommodation rooms. Parents are actively involved in their baby's care including feeding, diaper changes, and kangaroo care.

faq.question: What care do you provide for premature babies?

faq.question: Do you have emergency neonatal transport services?

faq.question: How often should I have antenatal checkups?
faq.answer: Generally, checkups are monthly until 28 weeks, every two weeks until 36 weeks, and then weekly until delivery. High-risk pregnancies may require more frequent monitoring.

faq.question: What tests are included in routine antenatal care?
faq.answer: Routine care includes blood tests, urine tests, ultrasound scans, blood pressure monitoring, and screening for conditions like gestational diabetes and preeclampsia.

faq.question: When should I start antenatal care?
faq.answer: Ideally, antenatal care should begin as soon as you know you are pregnant, preferably by 10-12 weeks of pregnancy for optimal monitoring and screening.

faq.question: What is included in high-risk pregnancy care?

faq.answer: We treat a wide range of pain conditions including chronic back and neck pain, arthritis, headaches, nerve pain, cancer pain, and post-surgical pain. Our multidisciplinary approach addresses both acute and chronic pain conditions.

faq.question: What is interventional pain management?
faq.answer: Interventional pain management involves minimally invasive procedures like nerve blocks, epidural injections, and radiofrequency ablation to diagnose and treat pain conditions. These techniques provide targeted relief with minimal side effects.

faq.question: How long does pain relief last after treatment?
faq.answer: Duration varies by treatment type and individual response. Nerve blocks may provide relief for weeks to months, while radiofrequency ablation can last 6-12 months or longer. Our team will discuss expected outcomes during consultation.

faq.question: Do you provide non-medication pain management options?
faq.answer: Yes, we offer comprehensive non-pharmacological treatments including physical therapy, nerve blocks, radiofrequency procedures, spinal cord stimulation, and behavioral therapy as part of our holistic approach.

faq.question: When should we seek help for infertility?
faq.answer: It is generally recommended to consult a fertility specialist if you have been unable to conceive after one year of regular, unprotected intercourse (or after six months if the woman is over 35).

faq.question: What are the first steps in infertility treatment?
faq.answer: The first step is a comprehensive evaluation of both partners, which may include hormone testing, semen analysis, and imaging tests to identify the cause of infertility. Based on the results, a personalized treatment plan is created.

faq.question: How long does infertility treatment take?
faq.answer: Treatment duration varies depending on the cause and type of infertility. Simple treatments may take a few months, while complex cases requiring multiple procedures may take longer. We provide personalized timelines for each case.

faq.question: Is infertility treatment covered by insurance?
faq.answer: Coverage varies by insurance provider and policy. We recommend checking with your insurance company about fertility treatment coverage and can provide detailed treatment cost estimates.

faq.question: How should I prepare for an endoscopy procedure?
faq.answer: Preparation varies by procedure type. For upper endoscopy, fast for 8-12 hours. For colonoscopy, follow specific bowel preparation instructions. Our team will provide detailed preparation guidelines.

faq.question: Is sedation used during endoscopic procedures?
faq.answer: Most patients receive conscious sedation to ensure comfort during procedures. Our anesthesia team monitors you throughout to ensure safety and comfort.

faq.question: How long does an endoscopy procedure take?
faq.answer: Upper endoscopy typically takes 15-30 minutes, while colonoscopy takes 30-60 minutes. Recovery time is usually 1-2 hours depending on sedation used.

faq.question: When will I receive my endoscopy results?
faq.answer: Preliminary results are available immediately after the procedure. If biopsies are taken, pathology results are typically available within 3-5 business days.

faq.question: What is hysteroscopy and when is it recommended?
faq.answer: Hysteroscopy is a minimally invasive procedure to examine and treat the inside of the uterus. It's recommended for abnormal bleeding, polyps, fibroids, fertility issues, and diagnostic purposes.

faq.question: Is hysteroscopy painful?
faq.answer: Most hysteroscopic procedures cause minimal discomfort. Office-based diagnostic hysteroscopy typically requires no anesthesia, while operative procedures may use local or light sedation.

faq.question: How long is the recovery time after hysteroscopy?
faq.answer: Recovery is typically quick. Most patients can return to normal activities within 1-2 days for diagnostic procedures and 3-5 days for operative procedures.

faq.question: Can hysteroscopy help with fertility issues?
faq.answer: Yes, hysteroscopy can identify and treat uterine factors affecting fertility such as polyps, fibroids, septum, and adhesions, potentially improving conception rates.
